headline: Cobalt Survey overstates nothing — its market slide makes no claim at all — and that is the problem: there is not enough evidence here to support a positive or a negative judgement, and no reliable public estimate exists for the market it is entering.

verdict.confidence_rationale: Low confidence is the finding, not a hedge. The deck makes one market statement — 'we believe this is a large and underserved market' — which is a belief with no figure, no segment and no source. The only research available says no reliable public estimate exists for spend on field data collection software specifically, because it is bundled into broader project management or captured as internal IT cost [S1]. So the central question cannot be answered from outside, and the deck supplies nothing from inside. LEAN NO reflects insufficient evidence to proceed, not evidence of a bad business, and it should flip on a single conversation that supplies what six slides did not.

scorecard.rationale: Slide 4 reads in full: 'We believe this is a large and underserved market.' No figure, no segment, no source. The research cannot fill the gap: no reliable public estimate exists for spend on field data collection software specifically, since it is typically bundled into broader project management software or captured as internal IT cost [S1]. That makes the sizing genuinely unknowable from public sources — which is a legitimate position for a pre-seed company, but only if the founders replace it with bottom-up evidence from their own pilots, and they have not.
evidence: No reliable public estimate exists for field data collection software spend [S1]

scorecard.rationale: There is no competition slide. The research does not name any vendor in this category either, so no specific competitor can be established — but the absence of a competition slide in a category with obvious mobile-forms and survey tooling is a gap in the deck rather than a gap in the market. Scored low for the omission, not for any demonstrated competitive threat.
evidence: No competition slide in the deck
No competitor named in the available research

scorecard.rationale: 'An offline-first mobile app that syncs when signal returns' is one sentence, and it is at least a real technical position for field work in remote sites. Whether offline-first is a differentiator or table stakes in this category is not established by anything available. No moat claimed.
No pricing, no revenue model, no unit economics. With three pilots and no revenue, there is no evidence that a price has ever been discussed.

Three pilot customers and no revenue. For a pre-seed raise of $750k on a SAFE this should not be marked down for thin revenue — that is the stage. What it should be marked on is thin evidence of demand, and it is thin: no conversion intent from the pilots, no stated willingness to pay, no usage data, no letters of intent. Three pilots are a starting point; the deck does not say what they showed.
evidence: Deck slide 5: three pilot customers, no revenue yet
No pilot outcomes, conversion intent or usage data given

scorecard.rationale: No team information of any kind. At pre-seed, with no revenue and no market sizing, the team is very nearly the entire investment case, and it is absent.
$750k on a SAFE is a normal pre-seed instrument and a reasonable amount. No cap is given, no use of funds, and no milestone the round is meant to reach — so there is nothing to judge the ask against.
evidence: Deck slide 6: raising $750k on a SAFE
No cap, use of funds or milestones

claim_audit.claim: We believe this is a large and underserved market
claim_audit.market_evidence: No reliable public estimate exists for spend on field data collection software specifically; it is typically bundled into broader project management software or captured as internal IT cost [S1]. The environmental consulting sector itself is highly fragmented [S1].
claim_audit.delta: The claim contains no figure to be distant from. The research cannot confirm or refute it, and says why: the spend is not separately measured. 'Underserved' is likewise untested — no source names a vendor serving this category or failing to.
claim_audit.so_what: This is the deck's only market claim and it cannot be checked from public sources. The correct response is not to score it down as overstatement but to require the founders to replace it with bottom-up evidence: how many consultancies, what they currently spend, what the three pilots would pay.

claim_audit.claim: Environmental consultants collect site data on paper and re-enter it later
claim_audit.market_evidence: No source addresses field data collection practice in environmental consulting. The sector is described as highly fragmented [S1], which is consistent with uneven tooling but does not establish the practice.
claim_audit.delta: Plausible and specific, but nothing available speaks to it.
claim_audit.so_what: This is the foundation of the whole business and it rests entirely on the founders' assertion. The three pilots are the obvious place to evidence it.

claim_audit.claim: Three pilot customers. No revenue yet.
claim_audit.delta: Cannot be checked externally. Stated plainly and without embellishment, which is to the deck's credit.
claim_audit.so_what: The value is in what the pilots showed, and the deck does not say. Ask for outcomes and conversion intent.

claim_audit.claim: An offline-first mobile app that syncs when signal returns
claim_audit.market_evidence: No source addresses product capability or vendor offerings in this category.
claim_audit.delta: Nothing available establishes whether this is differentiating or standard.
claim_audit.so_what: Worth establishing early, because if offline-first is table stakes the deck has no stated differentiator at all.

claim_audit.market_evidence: No source addresses pre-seed terms in this category.
claim_audit.delta: A normal instrument and a normal amount for the stage. No cap disclosed.
claim_audit.so_what: Ask for the cap and what the money is meant to prove.

where_deck_matches_market: The deck claims no figure the research contradicts. Nothing here is overstated, and that should be recorded as a positive rather than passed over — the failure mode in this deck is silence, not inflation.
The fragmentation of the environmental consulting sector [S1] is consistent with the deck's premise that tooling is uneven, though it does not confirm it.
where_deck_overstates: Nothing. There is no quantitative claim in this deck to overstate. The single market sentence is explicitly framed as a belief.
where_deck_understates: The pilots. Three deployed pilots is the only real evidence in the deck and it gets seven words. What the pilots showed — time saved, errors avoided, whether anyone offered to pay — is the entire case and is missing.

blind_spots.what: No reliable public estimate exists for spend on field data collection software specifically, because it is bundled into broader project management software or captured as internal IT cost.
blind_spots.why_it_matters: It means the deck cannot fix its market slide by finding a better analyst report — the number does not exist. The sizing has to be built bottom-up from consultancy counts and observed budgets, and the deck shows no awareness that this is the task.

blind_spots.what: The environmental consulting sector is highly fragmented.
blind_spots.why_it_matters: Fragmentation cuts both ways for a seller and the deck engages with neither: many small firms means a large number of potential customers, and also a long tail of small accounts, high cost of sale per unit of revenue, and no anchor customer to build on.

blind_spots.what: Where the budget currently sits — internal IT cost rather than a software line item.
blind_spots.why_it_matters: If the spend is captured as internal IT cost [S1], there may be no existing budget line to sell into, which is a materially different go-to-market from displacing an incumbent tool. Nothing in the deck addresses where the money would come from.

risks.risk: The market may be too small or too diffuse to support a venture outcome, and no public data can settle it
risks.mitigation_or_test: Require a bottom-up sizing: number of target consultancies, seats per firm, price per seat, built from the three pilots [S1].

risks.risk: There is no existing budget line, because the spend is currently internal IT cost
risks.mitigation_or_test: Ask each pilot who would sign the purchase order and out of which budget [S1].

risks.risk: Offline-first is table stakes rather than a differentiator
risks.mitigation_or_test: Ask what the pilots used before and why they stopped.

risks.risk: Pilots do not convert to paid
risks.mitigation_or_test: Ask for stated conversion intent and price from each pilot.

risks.risk: A fragmented buyer base gives a high cost of sale against small contract values
risks.mitigation_or_test: Ask what a typical consultancy would pay annually and what it costs to reach one [S1].

risks.risk: The team is entirely unknown at the stage where the team is the investment
risks.mitigation_or_test: Founder backgrounds and domain history, before anything else.

questions: What did the three pilots show — time saved, errors avoided, anything measured?
Would any of the three pay, and how much have they said?
How many environmental consultancies are you targeting, and how did you count them? [S1]
Who signs the purchase order, and is there an existing software budget or is this internal IT cost today? [S1]
What were the pilots using before your app?
Who is the team and what is your connection to this industry?
What is the SAFE cap, and what does $750k prove?
Is offline-first something the alternatives cannot do?

actions.action: Request founder backgrounds — at pre-seed with no revenue this is the investment case and it is absent
Request pilot outcomes and stated willingness to pay from all three
Ask for a bottom-up market build, since no public estimate exists to check against [S1]
Establish where the budget would come from given that spend is currently internal IT cost [S1]
Identify what the pilots used previously, to test whether offline-first differentiates

summary:
Cobalt Survey is a six-slide pre-seed deck for an offline-first mobile app that lets environmental consultants capture site data in the field instead of on paper. It has three pilot customers, no revenue, and is raising $750k on a SAFE.

This deck fails in the opposite direction from most. There is nothing here to contradict: slide 4, the market slide, reads in full 'We believe this is a large and underserved market.' No figure, no segment, no source, no methodology. That is not an inflated claim — it is the absence of a claim, and the two should not be scored the same way. A deck that says $88B when the number is $7B has told you something false. This deck has told you almost nothing at all.

The research cannot close the gap either, and that turns out to be the most useful thing it says. No reliable public estimate exists for spend on field data collection software specifically, because it is typically bundled into broader project management software or captured as internal IT cost [S1]. So the sizing is not merely missing from the deck, it is unavailable from public sources. Cobalt cannot fix slide 4 by finding a better analyst report. The number has to be built bottom-up — consultancy counts, seats, price — and nothing in the deck suggests the founders know that is the task in front of them.

The same source contains a second fact the deck does not engage with: the environmental consulting sector is highly fragmented [S1]. That cuts both ways. Many small firms means many potential customers and no gatekeeper, and it also means a long tail of small accounts, a high cost of sale per unit of revenue, and no anchor customer to build a reference base on. And if the spend today is captured as internal IT cost [S1], there may be no software budget line to sell into at all, which is a materially harder go-to-market than displacing a tool someone already pays for.

What the deck does have is three pilots, and it spends seven words on them. Whether those pilots saved time, avoided errors, or produced anyone willing to pay is the entire investment case, and none of it appears. For a pre-seed company, thin revenue is normal and should not be penalized; thin evidence of demand is the thing to weigh, and this is thin. There is also no team slide, no pricing, no competition slide and no use of funds.

The call is LEAN NO at low confidence, and the confidence figure is the honest part of the answer. There is not enough here to reach a considered positive or negative judgement, and anyone who reaches a confident one from six slides containing one belief and three pilots is overreaching. The single biggest reason for the lean is that the deck offers no evidence of demand beyond the assertion that the problem exists. What would flip it quickly: pilot outcomes with stated willingness to pay, a bottom-up market build to replace the belief on slide 4 [S1], and the founders' backgrounds. All three are a conversation away, which is why this reads as a deck that has not made its case rather than a company that cannot.
